text:
ConocoPhillips fell 1% today to $131.83, extending a slide that's seen the stock down nearly 3% over two weeks. The immediate pressure comes from conflicting Middle East signals: while Saudi Arabia is reportedly increasing crude supplies through the Strait of Hormuz to offset pipeline damage, fresh reports of flames near Riyadh's airport on the 19th have reignited supply-disruption concerns. Oil prices themselves remain volatile—US crude at $107 is well above pre-conflict levels but has given back gains as markets weigh whether new Saudi supplies will actually flow without further interruption.

The broader drag reflects a classic oil-market tension: energy companies benefit from higher prices, but only if those prices stick. The whipsaw between "supply will be disrupted" and "supply will be restored" means traders are unwilling to commit strongly in either direction, leaving refiners and producers like ConocoPhillips vulnerable to daily headline shifts rather than sustained conviction about fundamentals.
